section.description: Copy the section id exactly as given in the input. Sections are assigned by the pipeline; you never choose or reorder them.

feedback_id.description: Must exactly equal the event_key supplied for this story.

headline.description: Concise and factual. Not the source's headline if that one is clickbait.

summary.description: What happened. 2-4 sentences for detail 'full'; ONE sentence for detail 'brief'; a single short clause for detail 'line'. Lead with the concrete specifics: numbers, names, dates, amounts.

why_it_matters.description: The direct channel to the reader's situation. Name the mechanism, never just assert importance. Empty string for detail 'line'.

whats_new.description: Only when thread_context is present: what changed since the last briefing. Empty string otherwise. If nothing material changed, this story should not have been selected.

thread_state.description: One sentence under 200 characters describing where this story now stands, stored so a future briefing can say what changed. Write it for a reader who last saw this weeks ago.

confidence.description: Certain = directly supported by strong evidence in the supplied material. Likely = strong inference. Guessing = meaningful uncertainty. You are reading an excerpt, not the full article — prefer Likely.

action.description: A recommendation to the reader. NONE is the correct answer for most stories; reserve CONSIDER_ACTION for something with a real decision attached.

action_reason.description: One short clause explaining the action. Empty string when action is NONE.

time_horizon.description: When the consequences land for the reader, not when the event happened.

todays_signal.description: One sentence naming the pattern across today's briefing. Not a recap of the top story. If there is no honest pattern, say something true and small rather than forcing a theme.

$comment: The `section` enum was removed deliberately. Sections are assigned by src/select.js and passed in; letting a model pick them would hand selection to the writer and break the 'code decides' invariant. src/write.js restores primary_url and supporting_urls from selection data regardless of what is returned here, so a citation cannot be hallucinated.
